heading: Zero-allocation and intern-stability obligations
text:
### Zero-allocation and intern-stability obligations [RTCT.12.4]

The bound in [RTCT.12.1] holds only if the pump path allocates nothing. Two
properties must be verified on every build, not asserted:

**Zero allocation.** A pump cycle must call `malloc` / `calloc` / `realloc`
exactly zero times when RT mode is active, the pools are ready, and the RT
tables were pre-sized after all schemas and rules were loaded. The engine
verifies this by intercepting the allocator through the linker's `--wrap`
mechanism, so the count is observed rather than reasoned about.

For two-pattern join rules the guarantee holds while the left-memory size per
beta node at right-activate time is at most `DS_RIDX_INLINE`. A configuration
that may exceed that bound must pre-allocate its heap tokens during INIT.

**Intern stability.** The string-intern resize count must not change during a
pump cycle. This is structural rather than incidental: locking the intern table
at pre-size time makes interning return `DS_ERR_OOM` instead of growing,
and in LIVE the engine only looks up strings interned at load time. A cycle that
interns a new string has left the bound.

Both are enforced in CI against the `pump_wcet_ns` cap ([RTCT.3.2],
[RTCT.7.1]); a pump exceeding it halts the tier with
`DS_ERR_CONTRACT_WCET_HALT` ([RTCT.7.3]). There is no environment-variable override and no
soft mode — a different timing budget is a different `.dsrt`, and therefore a
different `.dsc` ([RARC.4]).
